description:
FILED s448 (Fable, round-6 review of agent P; found by an own-probe misfire, unrelated to P's diff).  PRE-EXISTING on main 922675a.

REPRO (minimal, probed):
    my @t = (1,2) if 0; print "b\n";
        perl: prints b (legal, no warning on 5.40.3)
        PCL:  the my-statement DROPS (;; PARSE ERROR: Bug. Fell through. Missing case: [PPIreference, ...]) and since the flip DIES at run time: 'PCL: statement not supported ... my @t = ... if 0'

DISCRIMINATOR (measured): the SCALAR form 'my $x = 1 if 0' transpiles fine; the ARRAY form drops with ANY RHS ((1,2), g(), a method call).  So the gap is the statement-modifier arm of the ARRAY/LIST my-declaration lowering, not the modifier itself.

Note the value semantics if fixed: 'my $x = EXPR if COND' retaining values across calls is perl's documented 'deprecated, do not rely' territory -- match what perl DOES today (probe first; the false-COND case simply leaves the variable declared and empty at file scope).

BAR: the array form with false and true COND vs perl, the scalar inverse, unless spelling; corpus-diff; census row if the shape occurs in a population (grep the drop-harvest text).  Same family as the #335 / #259 fall-through shapes but a DIFFERENT arm -- do not fold without a probe.
DIAGNOSED s449s (Opus, agent S of round 7) â not fixed, out of the bundle's
budget, but the search is narrowed to ONE line.  Every claim below is probed.

WHAT IS AND IS NOT BROKEN:
  my $x = 1 if 0;                  WORKS (top level and in a sub)
  our @a = (1,2) if 1;             WORKS (top level and in a sub)
  @t = (1,2) if COND;  (no `my`)   WORKS
  my @t = (1,2) if COND;           DROPS, top level AND in a sub
  my %h = (a=>1) if COND;          DROPS, the same way
  my @t = (1,2) unless COND;       DROPS, the same way

So it is neither the modifier nor the container: it is the `my`-CONTAINER
DECLARATION with a modifier, and the `let` half is fine â the emitted CL shows
`(let ((@t (make-array 0 â¦))) <the drop>)`, so the block scanner declared the
name and only the statement lowering failed.

WHERE.  NOT `Pl::Parser::_process_variable_statement`'s in-sub `my` synth route
(~Pl/Parser.pm:2388) â instrumented with a warn, it never fires, because v2
lowers a PPI::Statement::Variable itself.  The site is the CONTAINER branch of
`Pl::Parser2::_lower_block` (the comment "-- my @a / my %h / my (LIST) [= INIT];
â fresh containers in a let", ~Pl/Parser2.pm:8225).  It builds

    my @k = _strip_semi($first->schildren);

and hands the WHOLE run to `$self->_lower_expr([@k], $first)` â v1's expression
machinery, which parses `my @a = â¦` as one expression.  With a trailing
modifier the run is `my @t = (1,2) if 0`, which is not an expression, so PExpr
answers "Bug. Fell through. Missing case: [PPIreference, PPIreference(funcall)]"
â the `@t` and the `(1,2)` with the `=` and the `if` unaccounted for.

The SCALAR branch of the same sub does the missing step, ~112 lines earlier:

    my ($iexpr, $imod, $icond) = _split_modifier($init);
    $init = @$iexpr ? $iexpr : undef if defined $imod;
    ... return $self->_fallback_stmt(...) if _modifier_needs_fallback($imod);

and `our` gets it from `Pl::Parser::_process_our_declaration`'s synth route
(Pl/Parser.pm:2745), which strips the declarator and re-runs the rest through
the expression-statement path â the s410 fix whose own comment says
`our @a = (1,2) if 1` "emitted a PARSE ERROR into the assignment" before it.

SHAPE: split the modifier ONCE where `@k` is built, not at each use â the
container branch calls `_lower_expr([@k], $first)` at SIX sites (the chained-
declarator path, the self-ref single-container path, the self-ref list path,
the renamed/promoted path, and the plain path), and a per-site split is the
rule-11 smell.  `_modifier_needs_fallback` (while/until/for/foreach) must be
honoured as the scalar branch does; the value semantics are perl's documented
"deprecated, do not rely" territory only for the STATIC-variable reading, and
the probe says the false-condition case simply leaves the container declared
and empty, which the `let` already gives.

BAR (unchanged, plus): the six shapes above vs perl; the two `_split_modifier`
negatives `my @a = (1,2), 3;` and `my @a = (f 1, 2);` (a low-precedence tail is
NOT a modifier and the container branch already has a comment about that
distinction); corpus-diff; the drop-harvest text for the shape in a population.


DONE s451y (Opus, round 10 agent Y), commit f01d639.  Agent S's diagnosis was exactly right: the split goes ONCE where @k is built.  It also has to precede _multi_decl (which gained an optional token-list argument), because the NO-INIT spelling `my %h if 1` was a WHOLE-FILE die, not a drop.  One $assign_form closure feeds the five _lower_expr([@k]) sites; the let is unconditional and only the assignment is wrapped (probed: a false condition leaves the container declared and EMPTY and never evaluates the RHS); a no-init decl still runs its CONDITION in void (@kmod_eval -- NAME IT APART from the scalar branch's @declmod_eval, or perl's shadow warning on stderr fails a gate row, which is how this was caught).  45 probes vs perl.  Corpus-diff IDENTICAL over 111 and a 1007-file A/B SAME 1007 / DIFF 0 / RCDIFF 0.  Guard Pl/t/stmt-modifier-01.t 30 -> 39 (its own section 5), inverse-run verified.  DELIBERATE RESIDUE, filed as #722: a SELF-REFERENTIAL init under a modifier keeps DROPPING -- the fix puts the modifier BACK on the run there, because those shapes fuse the RHS into the `let` BINDING and a modifier would need two binding values.
subject: a CONTAINER `my` declaration with a statement modifier drops: `my @t = (1,2) if COND` (the no-init `my %h if 1` died the whole file)
